690660.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The browser window is 1440 px wide with the zoom at 100%, and the design pictures "sbr-03-b-sbr-expanded.png" (board 4.3), "sbr-10-a4-sbr-expanded-type.png" (board 4.10), "sbr-11-a4-export-csv.png" (board 4.11) and "sbr-12-a4-export-pdf-crop-1.png" (board 4.12) attached to this case are open beside it at 100% (actual size). Names, numbers and dates in the pictures are sample data.
  • Two active staff members at {Location-A} have their "Sales Representative" switch on: {Sales-rep-A} and {Sales-rep-B}.
    For example: {Sales-rep-A} is ZZAUTOTEST Ann Able and {Sales-rep-B} is ZZAUTOTEST Ben Able.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has no sales representative.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST SSR Fleet.
  • Part sale {Part-sale-1} for {Customer-A} has Sales Representative {Sales-rep-A}, one part and no labor, and was invoiced today.
    For example: {Part-sale-1} is P-30001 with one part sold at $50.00.
  • Starting screen: Reports > Sales By Representative is open in that browser window, with the date range set to today, Show Unassigned on and the Sales Type column turned on.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
690660.custom_steps:
1. Expand {Sales-rep-A} and compare {Part-sale-1}'s row with the picture of board 4.10.
  2. Export the Expanded CSV and read the same row's Hrs Worked, Hrs Invoiced, Labor Delta, Labor Invoiced and Labor Margin cells.
  3. Export the Expanded PDF and read the same cells.
690660.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: {Part-sale-1} shows as one row with Sales Type "Part Sales"; in the Labor Delta, Labor Invoiced and Labor Margin columns each cell shows a dash ("—"), as in the picture (today's report, board 4.3, shows 0.00 and $0.00 there).
  • Step 2: those cells are blank, as in the picture of board 4.11.
  • Step 3: those cells show a dash, as in the picture of board 4.12.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 11 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11269 (Story 5, Credit each side on the invoice and in Sales By Representative)

  • S5-R9: “A part sale is one "Part Sales" row holding every dollar of the invoice.”
  • S5-R3: “The report reads every invoice as one row per representative per Sales Type: "Labor" for a work order's labor side, "Parts" for its parts side, and "Part Sales" for a part sale.”
  • S5-R15b: “On a Part Sales row, Labor Delta, Labor Invoiced and Labor Margin, and the labor and hours cells of the Expanded downloads, show a dash on screen and in the PDF and are blank in the CSV. A part sale has no labor, so these columns don't apply to it.”

From: Chris Ward's answers to the Splitting Sales Representatives question sheet (answers 1 to 38, 19 Oct 2026; answers 39 and 40, 21 Oct 2026), Google Sheet 17Ry1BtRTPEkecBP5TlgAE0T93Ai1TQewdJ7B7WpWDBQ, tab "Questions for Chris", row 46, read 22 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward's answer 39: “39. (a) A dash on screen and in the PDF, and an empty cell in the CSV, as the design shows. A part sale has no labor, so the labor columns don't apply to it; it's the same rule as answers 24 and 25. This changes today's 0.00 / $0.00, so it's now listed under Release day. New S5-R15b, PRD v11.”

690664.custom_steps:
1. Expand {Sales-rep-A}.
  2. Expand {Sales-rep-B}.
  3. Export the Expanded CSV and read the Adjustments cells of the same two rows.
  4. Export the Expanded PDF and read the Adjustments cells of the same two rows.
690664.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: {Work-order-1}'s invoice shows one Labor row under {Sales-rep-A}; its Adjustments reads ($30.00) (600 ÷ 1,000 × 50), and the $30.00 shop supplies sit on the Labor row.
  • Step 2: {Work-order-1}'s invoice shows one Parts row under {Sales-rep-B}; its Adjustments reads ($20.00) (400 ÷ 1,000 × 50): each row shows only its own share.
  • Step 3: the CSV shows the same two shares under Adjustments: the $30.00 discount share on the Labor row and the $20.00 share on the Parts row.
  • Step 4: the PDF shows the same two shares under Adjustments.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 11 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11269 (Story 5, Credit each side on the invoice and in Sales By Representative)

  • S5-R6: “Whole-invoice fees and discounts are shared between the Labor and the Parts rows in proportion to each side's labor or parts dollars after that side's line fees and discounts, measured by size whatever their sign. The adjustment that stops a non-taxable discount from taking the subtotal below zero is a whole-invoice amount and is shared the same way. Example: labor $600.00, parts $400.00, shop supplies $30.00, whole-invoice discount ($50.00). The Labor row gets $30.00 supplies and ($30.00); the Parts row gets ($20.00). Subtotals $600.00 and $380.00 add up to $980.00. Each row shows its share in its Adjustments column.”
  • S5-R3: “The report reads every invoice as one row per representative per Sales Type: "Labor" for a work order's labor side, "Parts" for its parts side, and "Part Sales" for a part sale.”

From: Chris Ward's answers, question sheet of 19 Oct 2026, Google Sheet 17Ry1BtRTPEkecBP5TlgAE0T93Ai1TQewdJ7B7WpWDBQ, tab "Questions for Chris", rows 6-43 (answered 19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 20 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward's answer 22: “22. (a) as the feature spec. Yes, the Sales By Representative definition changes to the row's share.”
